children: JD Sports Fashion delivered third-quarter sales broadly in line with expectations, while the new midpoint of its lowered guidance is where consensus is currently positioned, analysts at RBC Capital Markets write in a research note. The U.K. retailer said like-for-like sales for the quarter through October slid 2.6% on year to 2.91 billion pounds. The group now targets profit before tax and adjusted items between 700 million pounds and 750 million pounds for the fiscal year as a whole. The company should maintain its position as a preferred partner of major sportswear brands like Nike and Adidas given its retailing strengths, Richard Chamberlain and Manjari Dhar say. "However, the broader outlook for the sports fashion sector is challenging and sales trends are currently muted," the analysts add. (andrea.figueras@wsj.com)
